title: Layer-by-layer diagnosis: from the cable to the application

videos.script: Something is broken, and the report says only that it does not work. {{report}} There are two ways to go on from there. One is to change things until the problem goes away. The other is to ask one question at a time, and let each answer choose the next question. {{layers}} This lesson takes the second way through faults staged in the lab, one at a time. The first four are the everyday ones, from a dead cable up to a web server that stopped. {{faults}} Each fails in its own way, and the way it fails is the clue. A refusal in no time at all is a different fault from a timeout after three seconds, even when the error says the same words. {{clues}} The last case is the one worth the lesson. A tunnel between two offices carries small things and swallows large ones, and nothing reports an error. A web page opens. A download never finishes. {{tunnel}} You will find out why with tcpdump and ping, and fix it with two rules on the router. Then you will check the fix with the same test that found the fault. {{fix}}
